reason: Owner direction 2026-10-10: 'I want any warning messages to actually appear as the error and not something that a user won't understand, and in whatever color is appropriate.' The current message 'That is not valid JSON: <parser error>' uses developer language and is shown in an amber box.

changes.before: Pasting text that is not JSON shows "That is not valid JSON: ..." in a red box; a package with an unsupported output shows the server's message. Nothing is filed.
changes.after: Pasting text that is not a package shows a red error box (role alert) whose first sentence says in plain words what is wrong and what to do, with no developer terms (for example: "This isn't a valid application package. Check that you pasted the whole package file."), followed by the technical detail on a separate line. A package with an unsupported output shows a plain-language red error naming the output that cannot be imported. Nothing is filed.
changes.tracesTo: Owner direction 2026-10-10 (plain-language errors, colour by severity); definition.json specGovernance.reviewChecklist rule 'Errors are plain and coloured by severity'
changes.whyNeeded: The owner set the rule for how errors read and look; the step must require it.
